result.markdown: # Finale: Publication Polish with patchwork, ggrepel & ggtext {#ggplot2-finale-polish} In this chapter, we will combine multi-plot layouts (`patchwork`), collision-free labels (`ggrepel`) and rich text (`ggtext`) into three polished before/after case studies. :::{.callout-note} ## Why this matters Individual plots answer single questions. Combining them into one composed figure with clean labels is what separates an exploratory chart from a published one. ::: :::{.callout-warning} ## Common pitfall Each extension adds load time and new syntax. Master core ggplot2 first; reach for these only for final figures. ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Case 1: Multi-Plot Layout Before: two related plots shown separately. After: one composed figure with a shared title. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(disp, mpg, color = factor(cyl))) + labs(title = "Displacement vs mileage") p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(factor(cyl), mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) + labs(title = "Mileage by cylinders") p1 + p2 + plot_annotation(title = "Engine size explains fuel economy") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ggplot2-finale-polish_files/figure-html/fin1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: Stack vertically with `/` and collect legends with `plot_layout(guides = "collect")`: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} p1 / p2 + plot_layout(guides = "collect") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ggplot2-finale-polish_files/figure-html/fin2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: ## Case 2: Collision-Free Labels Before: `geom_text()` labels pile onto each other. After: `geom_text_repel()` pushes them apart with thin leader lines. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} cars <- mtcars cars$model <- rownames(mtcars) efficient <- cars[cars$mpg > 30, ] ggplot(cars) + geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = efficient, aes(disp, mpg, label = model), size = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ggplot2-finale-polish_files/figure-html/fin3-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: ## Case 3: Rich Text Titles Before: plain titles. After: `element_markdown()` renders color and emphasis inline. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(disp, mpg, color = factor(cyl))) + labs(title = "Heavier engines drink more fuel") + theme(plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ggplot2-finale-polish_files/figure-html/fin4-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1344} ::: ::: ## Where to go next {.unnumbered} - patchwork reference for nested and tagged layouts - ggrepel and ggtext references for label-heavy figures - Export chapter to save the composed figure at print resolution
